chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abdillah, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who has intercourse with his wife: may he sleep in that state?
He عليه السلام said: “Indeed Allah, Exalted is He, takes the souls during their sleep, and he does not know what affliction may come upon him. When he has finished, then let him perform ghusl.”
I said: May the junub eat before performing wudu (ablution)? He عليه السلام said: “We do at times become lax, but let him wash his hand, and wudu (ablution) is better.”

key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in the state of janabah
key_terms.فَلْيَغْتَسِلْ: then let him perform ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.يَتَوَفَّى: takes the souls, referring to death or seizure of the soul during sleep

ai.seo_question: Can a person in janabah sleep or eat before performing ghusl or wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling and etiquette concerning janabah after intercourse. It encourages performing ghusl before sleep due to the uncertainty of death during sleep, and it permits eating before wudu (ablution) for the junub while stating that washing the hand is necessary and wudu (ablution) is preferable.
